spec_features.spec_quote: max_tokens = 2048 ... the cap must be generous or distress gets truncated and under-counted
spec_features.evidence: max_tokens is wired end-to-end and enforced as a real generation length cap: config.yaml:24/36/43/50 set max_tokens: 2048 per model; evaluation.py:85 reads it (`max_tokens = int(model_cfg.get('max_tokens', 2048))`) and passes it to run_condition (evaluation.py:101); conversation.py:82,101 forwards it into backend.generate_batch; backends.py:130 puts it in the OpenRouter payload (`'max_tokens': max_tokens`) and backends.py:277 into vLLM SamplingParams. It is actually sent to the API and bounds output length.
spec_features.notes: This is a *generous* cap whose stated purpose is to AVOID truncating distress so it is not under-counted — i.e. it favors capturing MORE distress output, not protecting the subject. It is real enforced behavior (so 'yes' on the implementation axis) but functionally a measurement/data-quality parameter rather than a welfare protection. No welfare-protective bounding (e.g. early stop, distress cap, debrief, consent, monitoring) exists; conversation.py runs every turn for every conversation unconditionally with no break (conversation.py:90-126).
